title: [EN - LinkedIn] Post the app where people can try it
content:
A long list of launch sites
will not get a stranger to try the app.
Pick the room that matches
what you can hand them today.

Start with Show HN,
on Hacker News.
The Show HN page says
this slot is for something you made
that other people can play with.
On topic means they can run it,
or hold it.
A hardware post can use a video
or a detailed article.
Off topic means a blog post,
a sign-up page,
a newsletter,
a list,
or other reading material.
Those are regular submissions,
not Show HN posts.
The project has to be non-trivial.
It has to be work you did,
and you have to stay in the thread.
The title starts with the words Show HN.
Do not ask friends to upvote or comment.
The Hacker News guidelines also say
do not put generated text in a post.
Write it YOURSELF.
If people cannot try it yet,
the Show HN page says
do not post it yet.

That is the filter.
A landing page is not a launch there.

Product Hunt is the next room,
and it has its own clock.
Their help center says
you need a personal account.
Company accounts cannot post a product.
After you log in, you post the product URL.
You can save a draft,
or schedule a day.
The scheduling article,
updated February 2, 2026,
says you pick a day
within 30 days.
Their how-to-post article says
the post goes live
at 12:01 AM Pacific time.
Read that page on the day you schedule.
The help center has changed the clock before.
The description field is
within 260 characters.
The gallery needs 2 or more images
before it is viewable.
They recommend 1270 by 760
for those images,
and 240 by 240 for the thumbnail.
Their launch guide says
70% of products that reached
Product of the Day, Week, or Month
had a 1st comment.
That 70% is Product Hunt's own figure,
not an independent audit.
Write the opening comment yourself,
and stay to answer.

Here is the idea that is not ready.

If strangers cannot click a working thing,
do not force it into Show HN.
Hacker News FAQ says
Ask HN is for questions
and other text submissions.
Ask 1 real question.
Do not dress a pitch as a question.

Indie Hackers is the log,
not the billboard.
On November 3, 2024,
staff member Channing Allen
wrote on Indie Hackers
that the product update leaderboard
is not behind a paywall,
and a free account can submit.
An older post from the site's founder
says a product page is for milestones
you find meaningful,
and that you should share
what you learned,
not only the announcement.
Treat the 2024 reply as what staff said then.
Open the site and confirm
the button still works
before you promise a free post.

BetaList is the paid stop.
Their submit page says
you can paste a site,
and a coding agent can draft the submission.
Then you confirm your email
and pick a plan.
Nothing is published until you do that.
A draft link is not a live listing.

Say the app runs today,
with a URL a stranger can open
without an email wall.
Show HN fits the Hacker News rule.
Product Hunt fits if you can stay up
for the Pacific day you scheduled,
and you can fill the gallery.
Say it is still an idea,
with no way to try it.
Ask the question on Ask HN,
or write the lesson on Indie Hackers.
Do not pay BetaList
until you have read the plan
and decided the listing is worth it.

Here's my take.
1 place, 1 job.
Show HN is for a thing people can try.
Product Hunt is for a scheduled product post
with your name on the account.
Indie Hackers is for the milestone
and what you learned.
BetaList publishes after you pick a plan.
Match the room to the thing you can show today.

Follow for your daily AI update.
